text:
Theo: Quick micro-sync — we need an SDR-ready battlecard + two bench narrative blurbs focused on positioning vs cloud AI and infra vendors. Keep it scannable (<1 page).

Rina: Required outputs: 3 headline claims, 3 one-line rebuttals, two bench storylines (method + 'typical outcome' only), SDR script (15s elevator, 30s pitch), and routing automation notes for Intercom.

Dasha: New twist — include a one-line "demo failure script" SDRs can reference when running the live demo (e.g., intentional canary fail to show fallback). Keep language non-technical for outreach.

Matt: My suggested hero claims (short):
- "Serve where you need it" (single API, multiple deployment guarantees)
- "Predictable inference economics" (workload-aware levers: batching, KV cache, quantization)
- "Rollouts that keep you online" (canary, routing fallback, region failover)

Theo: For cloud-AI rebuttals (30s):
- "We use cloud endpoints already" -> "Great — Redwood sits above them to give rollout safety, unified metrics, and predictable unit economics."
- "We already manage infra" -> "We can be hosted or private; Dedicated gives predictable capacity without rebuilding orchestration."
- "Compliance is a blocker" -> "Private control plane, KMS/HSM hooks, and auditable deploys."

Rina: Bench narratives (two short arcs):
- Chat-first SaaS: method = replay of 7-day production prompt set; typical outcome = batching + KV cache smooths p95 and reduces tail per-token cost.
- Spiky analytic ingest: method = staged spike tests with variable seq lengths + canary failover; typical outcome = routing + prewarmed pools preserve availability and avoid user-visible errors.

Dasha: SDR paste lines (copy/paste ready):
- 15s elevator: "Redwood gives one runtime to run LLMs hosted, reserved, or private so your app keeps predictable latency & cost."
- 30s pitch: "We layer rollout safety (canary & rollback), routing policies, and unit-cost levers like batching and KV caching so you can ship features without firefighting. Many teams keep their cloud endpoints but add Redwood for safer rollouts and better observability."

Matt: Demo-failure script (1 line for demo operator): "Trigger a canary variant that returns a slow response -> show automatic routing to hosted-compatible variant -> confirm user sees degraded but functional output."

Rina: Intercom routing rules (short): tag leads as = demo | dedicated-interest | tech-eval. Automation: dedicated-interest -> assign SE + high-touch SDR; tech-eval -> auto-send bench notebook + invite to private eval Slack. Add UTM rule: if utm_campaign=benchmark -> bump to high priority.

Theo: Webinar plan (tight): 3m positioning, 6m bench methodology (link to notebook), 10m scripted demo (force fallback), 10m panel Q&A, 1m CTA. Have the demo intentionally fail once.

webinar-bot: Landing page published -> /events/serve-with-confidence.

ops-bot: Recording room reserved Thursday 10:00 PT.

Dasha: Timeline: battlecard + elevator draft by Tue EOD; bench blurbs + methodology link by Wed; Intercom flows + SDR playbook by Fri.

Rina: I'll assemble the one-pager and add two tiny GIFs: canary trigger + fallback route.

Matt: I'll draft the three headline subject lines to test in the launch email.

Theo: Great. Keep the battlecard lean. I'll post the compiled draft to #marketing-drafts when it's ready. :rocket:
